name: Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha Temple
tagline: The hill shrine of Ayyappan and one of the world's largest annual pilgrimages
summary: Sabarimala, the hill shrine of Lord Ayyappa in Pathanamthitta: the pilgrimage season, the 18 sacred steps, the legend of Manikandan and pilgrim rules.
description: Sabarimala is a hill shrine in the Western Ghats dedicated to Lord Ayyappa (Dharma Sastha). It draws millions of pilgrims each year, most of them during the Mandala–Makaravilakku season from mid-November to mid-January.
Pilgrims traditionally observe a period of austerity (vratham), wear black or blue clothing, and climb the eighteen sacred steps carrying the irumudi, a two-compartment bundle of offerings.

folklore.title: Manikandan, the Pandalam Prince
story: Tradition says that a childless king of Pandalam found an infant with a bell (mani) around his neck on the banks of the river Pampa and named him Manikandan. After the king's wife later bore a son, court intrigue led the queen to feign an illness that only tiger's milk could cure.

Manikandan went into the forest, defeated the demoness Mahishi and returned riding a tigress at the head of a tiger pack, revealing his divinity. He asked that a shrine be built at Sabarimala, where he is worshipped as Ayyappa.
folklore.note: Retold from popular tradition; details vary by region.

highlights: Pilgrim trail via Erumely and Pampa
Strong tradition of inclusive, caste-free brotherhood among pilgrims (the 'Swami' greeting)

visitorInfo.bestTime: Pilgrimage season is mid-November to mid-January; the shrine also opens for the first five days of each Malayalam month. Check the official schedule before travelling.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Reach Pampa by road from Pathanamthitta, Kottayam or Kochi, then trek about 5 km uphill. Nearest railheads are Chengannur and Thiruvalla.
etiquette: Pilgrims follow a vratham (period of austerity) before the visit.
Follow the official darshan and online queue arrangements.
Carry only what you need; plastics are restricted in the forest area.
Respect the rules set by the Devaswom Board and the police on crowd management.
